how_to_read: Each feature lists what a source says it gives you, what it needs, the migration steps, and what nowinandroid did. A step is 'ran' (we ran it or committed data shows it; evidence linked), 'probe ready' (a probe can check it but we did not run that step alone) or 'docs only' (from the vendor page, not run).
cautions: Vendor numbers (for example the Gradle team's IDE sync times) are vendor-reported and are not shown here; nowinandroid has not been measured for them.
Isolated Projects counts are not strictly comparable across Gradle versions (deduplication from 9.4.0, warn mode change in 9.7.0).
AGP 10 statements quote Google's roadmap page, which calls its dates estimates. Nothing here adds to that page.
not_run: No step was run on a second AGP or Kotlin pairing (flag builds cover AGP 9.3.2 with Kotlin 2.3.0).
Isolated Projects was measured on configuration only (help), never on a full build.
No timing benefit was measured for any feature in this work.

features.name: Configuration cache
features.gives: Caches the result of the configuration phase and reuses it in later builds.
features.needs: Build logic that does not read the Project at execution time and follows the other configuration cache rules. Setting org.gradle.configuration-cache=true.
features.state: Stable. The Gradle manual calls it the preferred mode of execution since Gradle 9.0.0.
features.state_note: The manual page still says it becomes the default in Gradle 10; a newer Gradle post moved that to Gradle 11. No version is claimed here.

sources.title: Gradle manual: Configuration cache adoption guide

steps.action: Update Gradle to a recent version (the guide says CC quality improves with each minor release).
steps.check: ./gradlew --version; the harness records the pins per commit.

steps.action: Enable the cache and run only help (--configuration-cache).
steps.check: Log says "Configuration cache entry stored."; the probe reads the report.

steps.action: If it fails or misses, read the report (build/reports/configuration-cache/<hash>/<hash>/configuration-cache-report.html, not the Problems report).
steps.check: The probe returns each problem with message, task or build file, and line.

evidence.label: trimmed real reports in the repo test fixtures

steps.action: Fix build logic, dry-run and run the real dev loop, fix the rest, mark truly incompatible tasks.
steps.check: Problems reach 0 in the probe.

steps.action: Roll out to the team, then to CI.
steps.check: CI stays green with the cache on.

steps.action: Enforce with org.gradle.configuration-cache.problems=fail.
steps.check: The next violation fails the build.

nowinandroid.summary: Already in use in 2023, re-enabled after being switched off by mistake in 2024, used on CI in Dec 2024, enforced with problems=fail in Aug 2026. Zero problems on the 9 history commits that built.

events.what: Re-enabled (it had been switched off by mistake).
Used on CI, with the parallel option.
problems=warn changed to problems=fail, with a plugin bump that carried a fix.

features.name: Isolated Projects
features.gives: Aims at better scalability and performance, especially for large builds and IDE sync. Each project is isolated from the others.
features.needs: Build logic and plugins that do not reach into other projects. The manual says it uses the configuration cache infrastructure as its foundation.
features.state: Incubating since Gradle 9.7.0; the stable property names org.gradle.isolated-projects are preferred and the .unsafe names are deprecated.
features.state_note: Violations are deduplicated from Gradle 9.4.0, and from 9.7.0 --configuration-cache-problems=warn no longer turns them into warnings, so counts are not strictly comparable across Gradle versions. The Gradle team's own sync numbers are vendor-reported.

sources.title: Gradle blog: How the Gradle team adopted Isolated Projects

steps.action: Make the build configuration-cache compatible first.
steps.check: The configuration cache probe is pass.

steps.action: Try it: -Dorg.gradle.unsafe.isolated-projects=true --configuration-cache help (Gradle 9.7.0 and later prefer org.gradle.isolated-projects).
steps.check: The probe lists problems grouped by message, with the plugin class that caused each.

steps.action: Fix or switch off the violators: update the plugin, or skip the tool while Isolated Projects is on.
steps.check: Problem count drops.

evidence.label: nowinandroid 4a5becfc: 273 to 0 on the same Gradle 9.3.0

steps.action: Measure the gain. The manual says it only speeds up the configuration phase and suggests a "dangerously ignore problems" mode to estimate before fixing everything.
steps.check: Compare configuration-phase time with and without, using a Build Scan or profile report.

steps.action: Turn it on in gradle.properties.
steps.check: The probe stays at 0.

nowinandroid.summary: The build was made to pass in Feb 2026 and the property was turned on in Sept 2026. The switch changed nothing measurable because the count was already 0.

events.what: Made the build pass with Isolated Projects on: enabled KSP's support, skipped Spotless and the graph tasks when it is on. 273 problems to 0 (203 from the Spotless plugin, 70 from the project's own graph tasks).
Turned the property on. 0 problems before and after.

features.name: Built-in Kotlin
features.gives: No need to apply the org.jetbrains.kotlin.android plugin. Simpler build files, and fewer compatibility problems between AGP and that plugin.
features.needs: AGP 9.0 or higher. Remove the plugin, then migrate kapt, kotlinOptions {} and kotlin.sourceSets {} where they are used.
features.state: On by default in AGP 9.0. Temporary opt-out: android.builtInKotlin=false (the page says that also needs android.newDsl=false).
features.state_note: Google's roadmap page, which calls its dates estimates, says AGP 10.0 removes the opt-out flags.

steps.action: Upgrade to AGP 9.0 or higher. Built-in Kotlin is on by default.
steps.check: The android.builtInKotlin flag build passes with value true.

steps.action: Remove the org.jetbrains.kotlin.android plugin from module builds, or from the convention plugins that apply it.
steps.check: The build no longer fails with the "no longer required" error.

evidence.label: nowinandroid d46b9dc2 removed three applies, but that work-in-progress commit does not build

steps.action: Migrate kotlin-kapt, android.kotlinOptions {} and kotlin.sourceSets {} where used.
steps.check: Build passes; no deprecation warnings.

steps.action: If needed, opt out temporarily with android.builtInKotlin=false.
steps.check: The AGP deprecation probe shows the warning that names the removal.

nowinandroid.summary: The convention plugins stopped applying the Kotlin Android plugin in a work-in-progress commit in Oct 2025. That commit does not build, so there is no clean before and after; the final state builds.

events.what: Removed three applies of the Kotlin Android plugin in the convention plugins (work in progress; does not build).

features.name: New DSL and Variant API
features.gives: A lazy model that works with the configuration cache. The Instrumentation API instruments each library as soon as it is ready and only re-instruments changed classes.
features.needs: Replace applicationVariants, libraryVariants, variantFilter and eager buildConfigField with androidComponents (onVariants, beforeVariants), Artifacts and Sources APIs. Third-party plugins must stop using the old types.
features.state: Roadmap page (dates are estimates): AGP 10.0 completes the move to a fully lazy model and enforces it.

steps.action: Run the AGP Upgrade Assistant in Android Studio.
steps.check: n/a (IDE)

steps.action: Upgrade to the latest AGP 9.x and fix its deprecation warnings. The page says the build should work without android.newDsl=false and android.builtInKotlin=false.
steps.check: The AGP deprecation probe shows 0 warnings.

steps.action: Replace the legacy variant APIs with androidComponents, Artifacts and Sources APIs.
steps.check: Flag builds with the legacy-API and new-DSL-interface flags at the future value pass.

steps.action: Update third-party plugins. The page says plugins that use legacy extension types fail with a ClassCastException.
steps.check: Build passes after the plugin bumps.

evidence.label: nowinandroid eee94e4b bumped the protobuf plugin

nowinandroid.summary: Opted out in Oct 2025 with a note about a blocker in the protobuf plugin, and opted back in in Jan 2026 after bumping that plugin. The AGP deprecation warning went from 1 to 0.

events.what: Removed the opt-out after bumping the protobuf plugin and moving one module off the Android library plugin.

features.name: Task configuration avoidance
features.gives: A registered task is known to the build but is not created or configured until it is needed, so unneeded tasks cost nothing.
features.needs: Use tasks.register and the lazy APIs in build logic and plugins instead of the eager ones.
features.state: Documented API with a migration guide.

sources.title: Gradle manual: Avoiding unnecessary task configuration

steps.action: Migrate tasks.all {} and tasks.withType(...) {} configuration.
steps.check: Fewer tasks created at configuration time; the Build Scan configuration performance tab shows eager and lazy tasks.

steps.action: Replace by-name lookups (getByName) with named.
steps.check: Same check.

steps.action: Replace create(...) with register(...).
steps.check: Same check.

steps.action: Measured on nowinandroid: how many tasks get realized.
steps.check: The task-realization lab in this repo.

nowinandroid.summary: tasks.register appears in the build logic from 2022 and tasks.create in places (a coverage setup in 2024). There is no single adoption commit.

features.name: Problems API
features.gives: Plugins report structured problems. They go into an HTML Problems Report, to the console (warnings with --warning-mode=all), and to IDEs as Tooling API events.
features.needs: Plugin authors adopt it. App teams read the report.

steps.action: Read the HTML Problems Report; the console prints its location at the end of the build.
steps.check: The harness saves problems-report.html per build; no feature probe reads it yet.

nowinandroid.summary: Not something an app team adopts.

features.name: Java toolchains and the Foojay resolver
features.gives: Gradle downloads and manages the required JDK. The same Java version is used to compile and run.
features.needs: A toolchain definition, plus a resolver plugin such as org.gradle.toolchains.foojay-resolver-convention in settings.

steps.action: Declare the toolchain in the build.
steps.check: ./gradlew javaToolchains lists detected toolchains (named on the manual page).

steps.action: Add a toolchain resolver in settings for auto-download.
steps.check: A clean machine builds without a local JDK.

nowinandroid.summary: Tried jvmToolchain in early 2023 and removed it in May 2023. No Foojay resolver at head.

features.name: AGP KMP library plugin
features.gives: A single-variant plugin for Kotlin Multiplatform libraries. The page says this simplifies configuration and improves build performance.
features.needs: AGP 8.10.0 and KGP 2.0.0 at least. No build types or product flavors; some features are opt-in or unsupported. A KMP module on com.android.library uses APIs the page says are deprecated in AGP 9.0 and expected to be removed in AGP 10.0.

steps.action: Declare the plugins in the version catalog and add them to the root build with apply false.
steps.check: Sync succeeds.

steps.action: Apply the plugin in the KMP library module and move the sources.
steps.check: Module builds.

steps.action: Check the limits (no build types or flavors). For a module that needs variants, the page recommends a separate com.android.library module.
steps.check: Build passes.

nowinandroid.summary: Not adopted. nowinandroid has no KMP library module, so it cannot be run there.

features.name: Kotlin Build Tools API
features.gives: One entry point to the Kotlin compiler for build systems: incremental compilation, compiler plugins, daemons.
features.needs: Direct use needs an opt-in (ExperimentalBuildToolsApi). It is a plugin and build-tool author feature.
features.state: Beta for Kotlin/JVM, Alpha for Kotlin/JS and Wasm.

nowinandroid.summary: Nothing for an app team to adopt.

features.name: Declarative Gradle
features.gives: A declarative build language, so tools can read how a build is configured without running imperative logic (Gradle's stated aim).
features.needs: Nothing an app team should do yet.
features.state: Experimental, in its third early-access preview.

nowinandroid.summary: Not adopted. A "watch" item, not a migration.
